item.title: Malicious node-ipc npm Packages Trigger New Supply Chain Security Alarm

Forensic artifacts: • Consistent timestamp "Oct. 26, 1985" across all malicious tarball files • Temporary archives stored at /nt-/.tar.gz (may persist if execution interrupted) • Environment variable __ntw used for execution path control

item.title: [Guest Diary] New Malware Libraries means New Signatures, (Fri, May 15th)
item.description:
Eight-year-old Outlaw/Shellbot campaign updates SSH client fingerprint to libssh 0.11.1, potentially evading hassh-based detection rules written against earlier versions while maintaining identical persistence tactics.
Key technical details: • New hassh fingerprint: 03a80b21afa810682a776a7d42e5e6fb (SSH-2.0-libssh_0.11.1) • Unchanged authorized_keys SHA-256: a8460f446be540410004b1a8db4083773fa46f7fe76fa84219c93daa1669f8f2 • Persistent "mdrfckr" comment string in SSH key since 2018 • 24 source IPs coordinated attack burst within 131-second window (April 19, 2026) • Same credential dictionary: steam:Steam29!, postgres:q1, dev:dev5, root:AAAaaa111
Attack methodology: • Brute force SSH with common credentials across multiple IPs (T1110.001) • Writes persistent SSH key to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys (T1098.004) • Executes chattr -ia .ssh; lockr -ia .ssh defensive disarm sequence • Competitor cleanup via /tmp/secure.sh script
This represents the third documented libssh version evolution (0.6.x → 0.9.x → 0.11.x). Detection rules relying on older hassh values 51cba57125523ce4b9db67714a90bf6e or f555226df1963d1d3c09daf865abdc9a will miss current activity.
Hunt for the unchanged SHA-256 hash and "mdrfckr" string rather than hassh values. Alert on multiple IPs targeting same accounts within short timeframes.

item.description:

DFIR artifacts: - Working directory with structured staging areas (Peeps, Autos, Result files, Task files, Logs) - Window class names matching module names (Bridge/Kernel/Worker) - Mailslot names: MD5 hash of "mailslot-" + module name - Protobuf message structures for inter-module communication

item.title: OrBit (Re)turns: Tracking an open-source Linux rootkit across four years of forks and deployments
item.description:
Four-year evolution of OrBit Linux rootkit reveals it's a fork of open-source Medusa toolkit, deployed by state-sponsored UNC3886, eCrime BLOCKADE SPIDER, and RHOMBUS botnet operators.
Deep technical breakdown of OrBit's development reveals sophisticated operator tradecraft:
• **Two parallel lineages identified**: Full-featured "Lineage A" (66+ exports, PAM harvesting, network hiding) and lite "Lineage B" (54 exports, reduced footprint for specific environments)
• **Source attribution confirmed**: OrBit samples contain unstripped symbols (rkld.c, rknet.c, rkload.c) matching Medusa GitHub repo structure exactly. XOR obfuscation scheme (keys 0xA2/0xAA) and build pipeline artifacts prove common origin
• **Multi-actor deployment spanning 2022-2026**: UNC3886 🇨🇳 state espionage (VMware/Juniper infrastructure), BLOCKADE SPIDER eCrime (Embargo ransomware), and RHOMBUS botnet operations with C2 at cf0[.]pw resolving to Russian 🇷🇺 infrastructure
• **2025 capability expansion**: New pam_sm_authenticate hook enables service-side PAM impersonation, two-stage infector architecture adds C2 communication via cron jobs, breaking from purely passive SSH backdoor model
• **Persistence mechanisms**: LD_PRELOAD via patched ld.so, installs to /lib/libseconf/, /lib/locate/, or /lib64/libseconf/ with hidden credential storage in sshpass.txt/sshpass2.txt
Hunt for XOR-decoded string tables in .
